title: Quintessentially Pillowy German Jerusalem Artichokes Gratin
description: A rich, pillowy German dessert featuring Jerusalem artichokes, topped with a crunchy rendered fat crust. Can be served warm or at room temperature.

ingredients.name: Rendered pork fat or beef tallow

instructions: Pierce the Jerusalem artichokes with a fork several times and bake for 30 minutes, or until tender.
Let the Jerusalem artichokes cool, then peel and slice them into 1/4-inch thick rounds.
In a medium saucepan, combine the heavy cream, granulated sugar, and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Remove the cream mixture from the heat and let it cool to room temperature.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and flour. Temper the egg yolks by slowly pouring the cooled cream mixture into the bowl, whisking constantly.
Add the sliced Jerusalem artichokes to the bowl and stir to coat.
Pour the mixture into a molcajete or other 1-quart baking dish.
Dot the top of the gratin with the unsalted butter and sprinkle with nutmeg.
Bake the gratin for 25-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the casserole is set.
Remove the gratin from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Drizzle the rendered pork fat or beef tallow over the top of the gratin and serve warm or at room temperature.
